output.brief:
Store 14's rise from 1.5% to 2.3% may not be a real change in losses. The interim figures are extrapolated from partial cycle counts, with an error of about ±0.6 points per quarter. Across past store-years, about half of "two consecutive rises" patterns were not confirmed by the year-end full count. Store 14's own full-count shrink has stayed at 1.5–1.8% for three years. The rise is spread evenly across all departments, and sales mix has not changed. That fits measurement noise more than a shift in mix. The rise does not clearly point to self-checkout or customer theft. The shoplifting log counts went up chain-wide when the incident app launched, so they aren't a reliable signal. The ethics tip was checked against CCTV and showed routine cardboard bale runs, so there is no basis to discipline the stocker. Neighbouring stores show no matching trend, but that doesn't settle the cause.

Next steps: keep store 14 in the 7 December full count, and don't confirm Operations' request to drop it. Hold off on a guard, pulling the lanes, or any personnel action until the count result is compared with the interim figures. I am moderately sure. I did not collect any evidence that could directly test the self-checkout or customer-theft explanations.
